content:
Nuevo Laredo will turn its clocks back one hour in the early hours of Sunday, November 1, joining more than 30 northern border municipalities in Mexico that adjust their time to stay in sync with the United States, according to El Congresista.

At 2:00 a.m. on November 1, clocks in those municipalities go back to 1:00 a.m. under Mexico's time-zone law, the report says. Residents are advised to make the change manually on the night of October 31; most electronic devices will update automatically.

In Tamaulipas, the municipalities making the change are Nuevo Laredo, Guerrero, Mier, Miguel Alemán, Camargo, Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, Reynosa, Río Bravo, Valle Hermoso and Matamoros, according to the report. The adjustment is meant to ease work and commercial activity across the border.

The rest of Mexico will not change its clocks: most of the country has stayed on standard time all year since daylight saving time was eliminated in most of the country in October 2022, the report says.

Sources:

  • El Congresista, "Cambio de horario 2026: municipios de frontera ajustan sus relojes," October 31, 2026
